speaker: Mr Abdul Samad
text: asked the Minister for Manpower whether he can provide an update on (i) the number of companies that successfully applied for the Capability Transfer Programme since it was first introduced and (ii) its assessment of the programme's effectiveness in terms of helping companies, associations and professional bodies to develop and acquire new capabilities for their Singaporean workforce.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what studies have been done on the take-up rate of the Capability Transfer Programme (CTP) by the different sectors; (b) how does the Government measure the CTP's success in achieving foreign-to-local skills transfer; and (c) whether the Government has considered imposing conditions on the funding of CTP, such as requiring the applicant company to meet targets for the reduction of foreign labour after a specified period of time.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The top three sectors in terms of the number of local trainees are Precision Engineering, Air Transport and Logistics.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Under the CTP, funding support is provided to companies to acquire global capabilities that are not available in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This can be done in a variety of ways, such as by: one, bringing foreign specialists into Singapore to train locals in new capabilities; two, sending locals for overseas training attachments; three, facilitating remote capability transfer from foreign specialists; and four, supporting follow-on training in Singapore by local specialists who were trained by foreign specialists or had trained overseas.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To qualify for funding, companies are required to submit a training plan on the new capabilities to be acquired and the number of local employees who will be trained.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This way, we ensure that each CTP project leads to genuine upskilling.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For example, the CTP project by SP Services Limited sent 12 local employees to the US to learn about advanced network design and optimisation.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Upon their return to Singapore, these employees, in turn, trained 13 other local colleagues.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As a result of this project, the local team is now able to take on an expanded job role, performing more advanced tasks, such as fault isolation and data analysis.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: These were previously jobs that could only be undertaken by contractors.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat also asked about conditions that are imposed on the CTP.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: CTP companies are required to commit to training a specific number of locals.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Such conditions would penalise companies that are transferring expertise to locals but, at the same time, still need to grow their overall workforce, both locals and foreigners, to meet growing demand.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Due to travel restrictions arising from COVID-19, take-up of the CTP has been minimal over the past two years.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: CTP is not the only way in which the Government supports firms in capability transfer.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Enterprise Singapore’s Global Ready Talent Programme supports Singapore companies in building a young talent pipeline through internships and overseas work opportunities.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: MOM is also piloting the Global Rotation Scheme, which facilitates the entry of high-potential employees from abroad, on the condition that these same companies post Singaporeans abroad on the same leadership development programme.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Beyond Government schemes, skills transfer takes place through structured company training programmes, as well as learning from a variety of people, including peers, superiors, customers and suppliers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Workers may also acquire valuable skills through a range of assignments, including overseas postings and even job changes, to gain exposure to different industries or markets.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We can see that this is reflected in the macro employment data.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Resident unemployment rates have remained low – they rose during the pandemic but have since recovered to 3.1% as at January 2022.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Real median income of full-time resident workers grew an average of 2.6% per year from 2011 to 2021.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I am glad to know from the Minister that there are more sectors now that are benefiting from the CTP – 20 sectors – and, hopefully, we will have more sectors, going forward.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My question is in regard to my Adjournment Motion which I raised in 2019 on this matter and I am raising it in the Parliamentary Question as well.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: With regard to the funding support for CTP, I had suggested before whether we can consider expanding CTP to support the transfer of capabilities from foreign employees currently already employed in Singapore to local employees, with the eventual aim of localising jobs, working in tandem with the localisation targets I mentioned back in the Adjournment Motion.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This is because the current funding support of CTP only applies to incoming foreign specialists.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, I hope the Minister can answer my question here, whether we can consider expanding CTP to support transfer of capabilities from foreign employees currently already employed in Singapore to local workers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: It is something that we, certainly, will look into closely.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think the appreciation of the fact that this has to be a very tightly-scoped funding support structure is important in making sure that capability transfers are effected and also effective, so that our local employees can gain the maximum amount of expertise and skillsets from this particular programme.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think this is of paramount importance to us.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, perhaps, a broad summary of how we think in terms of the extension of funding support.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Support levels will be determined by WSG in consultation with the relevant sector agencies.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Today, the funding rates, the different levels of support, serve and exist to differentiate the level of support based on the assessed impact of each project.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We also have to ensure that there is some degree of co-funding from the participating company or the industry.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Can MOM consider a higher funding for companies intending to embark on CTP and may also engage the unions through our Company Training Committee for a more balanced assessment, to ensure that there is a structured plan for a transfer of capabilities?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, we will continue to monitor the take-up of the scheme.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In the absence of additional feedback, unless Mr Abdul Samad is suggesting that there are instances where he finds that the funding cap of S$300,000 is restrictive, it is something that we can look to review.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I think this is a subject I spoke about in my Budget speech last year as well, seeking details on the number of individual Singaporeans who have benefited from CTP.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In view of the revision or the review of the ITMs towards ITM 2025, does CTP feature very prominently in the review?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Because as I mentioned last year, my view is it can be an important conduit through which locals upskill effectively with new skills that have a direct knock-on effect on their companies and, of course, on enterprise, in general.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: My second question is specifically on the 990 locals and the 140 companies that the Minister spoke of earlier.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: How many of them received the highest cap of funding at 90%?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The CTP is one of the multitude of programmes that we have available in ensuring that we are able to nuance the JTM to match what we have actually set out to achieve under our ITMs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I believe that the Minister for Trade and Industry, Mr Gan Kim Yong, will provide an update in terms of the effectiveness of the programmes at a later stage.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Suffice to say, we have got a whole host of other programmes like the Company Training Committee (CTC) programme administered by NTUC.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Then, WSG works on the Career Conversion Programme (CCP) in helping many of our mid-career job-seekers who want to switch careers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, it is one of the many programmes that we have available.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: One other point, and I hope that the Leader of the Opposition may want to take note, is that in the last two years during COVID-19, because of border restrictions, the number of companies applying for this particular programme to allow either their employees to go overseas for training or to bring foreign expertise here, has been significantly curtailed.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Hence, that speaks for the very low take-up rate over the last two years.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But as border controls ease, as we start opening up, I would expect that the numbers would start to go up again, all the way until the end of the programme in 2024.
